newsitem.title: CANADA: Domtar sees better forestry market in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Domtar sees better forestry market in Q4.

text.p: Pulp and paper firm Domtar Inc said it expected a better market for the rest of the year after third-quarter earnings were hit by weaker prices for all major products except softwood lumber.
"Market conditions are expected to improve moderately during the fourth quarter of 1996 as prices for pulp and fine papers products firm up, following sharp declines earlier this year," it said.
Domtar's third-quarter net profit dropped to C$8 million from year earlier C$91 million, which had been a record for the company.
Domtar said third-quarter earnings fell due to a soft market. "Average prices for all major products, except for softwood lumber, were lower than in the corresponding period last year," it said.

The last quarter is traditionally weak for Domtar as a slowdown in North American housing construction reduces lumber demand. "Shipments for most of the corporation's business are, however, expected to be lower in the fourth quarter compared to the third quarter due to seasonal factors," Domtar said.

"Given current economic forecasts, the corporation is confident that the continuing strength of the Canadian and United States economies will increase demand for its key product lines in 1997," Domtar added. The Canadian government will unveil its final quotas for softwood lumber shipment to the United States in November and Domtar is reviewing its operations to deal with the outcome. "The implementation of the new Canadian quota system for softwood lumber exports to the United States will affect part of our exports of this product to that country," it said.
"These measures include increased production of value-added lumber products, reconfiguration of our sawmill operations and the development of other export markets," it said.
Domtar said it planned to complete the modernization of its Lebel-sur-Quevillon, Quebec plant in 1997's first quarter.
